mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% in a 3-month window, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative feedback in corporate earnings expectations and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the prior month, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply chain recovery phase, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 index points indicates improving manufacturing output, boosting corporate margins and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances during supply chain recovery when INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the prior month signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS increases over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 3.0% year-over-year, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to delay rate cuts, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% indicates a tightening monetary policy cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery phase, a sustained increase in real sales (RSAFS) above 500,000 million dollars indicates strengthening consumer demand, driving corporate earnings growth and resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances during post-recession recovery when RSAFS exceeds 500,000 million dollars, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
